Të lidhura None found His daughter, Kaja Kallas, the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, announced the news. In a statement published on Saturday morning, she said that her father had died during the night. Siim Kallas was one of the leading figures in modern Estonian politics. He headed the Estonian government from 2002 to 2003, and during his career also served as Foreign Minister and Finance Minister. After his time as head of government, he continued his work in the institutions of the European Union. Kallas was a European commissioner from 2004 to 2014 and later served as Vice-President of the European Commission, where he was responsible, among other things, for the Transport portfolio. He also played a significant role in Estonia’s economic changes after the restoration of independence. He headed the Bank of Estonia from 1991 to 1995 and took part in the country’s monetary reform process. Kaja Kallas, his daughter, currently serves as the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and as Vice-President of the European Commission. THE Bishop of Worcester has travelled to Ukraine to share a message of solidarity and prayer from the Archbishop of Canterbury as the country marked 35 years of independence under the shadow of war. Bishop Hugh Nelson attended Ukraine’s National Prayer Breakfast in Kyiv on August 23. He joined President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukrainian church leaders, religious representatives, government officials, military personnel and international guests. The gathering took place on the eve of Ukraine’s Independence Day and focused on prayer for the country’s defenders, prisoners of war, peace and national unity. Bishop Hugh, who is also the Church of England’s Bishop to the Armed Forces, delivered a message from Archbishop of Canterbury Sarah Mullally. In it, she said the Church of England continued to stand in 'prayerful solidarity' with Ukraine, recognising the 'immense sacrifices' made to defend its people and the values of freedom and human dignity. The Archbishop rejected descriptions of the conflict as a 'holy war'. Quoting Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew, she said: “There has never been, nor will there be, a ‘holy war’. War is always a tragedy, never an expression of God’s will. We pray for peace.” She added: “We pray for those who have lost their lives, for those who mourn, for the wounded, the displaced, and all who live under the daily shadow of violence and fear. "May God grant you courage, wisdom and hope, and may the peace of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, guard your hearts and minds in the days ahead." Bishop Hugh arrived in Kyiv on Saturday after travelling overnight from Poland. During the visit, he met His Beatitude Metropolitan Epiphany, leader of the Orthodox Church of Ukraine, at the St Michael’s Monastery complex in Old Kyiv. He also visited the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra, a UNESCO World Heritage site that was damaged in a Russian drone and missile attack in June. The bishop is expected to meet Ukrainian military chaplains, combat veterans and a range of church and civic leaders during his time in the country. The Diocese of Worcester said Bishop Hugh’s visit was intended to demonstrate continuing support for the churches and people of Ukraine. Photograph: Hornbreak Fire Department US crime Man serving life sentence for murder escapes Tennessee prison, slipping through fence, officials say Security footage shows Jacob Morley escaping in his prison uniform, investigators describe Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email Guardian staff and agencies Tue 27 Oct 2026 09.20 EDT Last modified on Tue 27 Oct 2026 12.53 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Tennessee authorities on Tuesday were still searching for a convicted murderer who, investigators say, escaped a state prison by slipping through a fence and fleeing in a stolen truck. The state department of correction (TDOC) said in a statement that officials realized Jacob Morley, 28, was unaccounted for at about 11.30pm on Sunday at the Northwest correctional complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee . Investigators looked at security cameras and saw Morley escaped through a fence while wearing his prison uniform, officials said. They did not release any other details, including how Morley got through the fence. Surveillance video also reportedly showed Morley stealing a truck at about 1am on Monday. He was in the truck when video also recorded him passing in front of the Hornbeak fire department – about 15 miles from the correctional complex – at about 1.18am, the department said . Prison officials offered a reward of up to $2,500 for Morley’s arrest. They said law enforcement officials throughout the area had searched buildings and other structures near the prison about 90 miles (145km) north of Memphis in an isolated, rural area of flat land tucked near a bend in the Mississippi River close to Missouri. Morley is 5ft 11in (1.8 meters) and 240lb (109kg). He has brown hair and green eyes. Morley was sentenced to life for killing co-worker Cody Birchfield in 2022. Birchfield’s body was found in a box under Morley’s Carter county, Tennessee, home after he had been missing for a few weeks. Beside first-degree murder, Morley was also convicted of aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, vandalism and evading arrest. Morley had led police on a chase that ended in North Carolina when he saw officers at his home in 2022 in connection with Birchfield, authorities said. The north-west correctional complex has been the site of several reported violent attacks between inmates and by employees. In July, a grand jury handed up dozens of indictments for five inmate murders, assaults against staff and inmates and other violence at the complex. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion The prison can house 1,776 men and minors who have been convicted as adults, according to TDOC.
